campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 20, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Campbell City Council meeting listed a mix of community recognitions, routine approvals, and two larger items: a request to extend construction deadlines for the Pruneyard Center and a proposed equipment lease for the city's street-marking work. It also listed the introduction of the new Youth Commission and a roughly $2.75 million bills-and-claims approval.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a public hearing on the Pruneyard Center Association's request to extend phasing deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 (a five-story office building, parking structure expansions, and additional commercial buildings) and the related parcel map to December 31, 2031, with the Planning Commission recommending the Council approve it.
The agenda listed a proposed five-year, $159,327 lease with NCL Government Capital, through Sourcewell, for a thermoplastic melter trailer (TPM-1500).

The agenda listed recognitions for Code Enforcement Officer Appreciation Week (Oct. 11-17) and the Campbell Little League Senior All-Star Team, 2026 Northern California Senior League State Championship winners.
The agenda listed an introduction of the 2026-2027 Campbell Youth Commission, including a presentation of the commissioners' initial work plan.

The consent calendar listed approval of $2,750,402.16 in bills and claims, several sets of past meeting minutes, and adoption of the city's job classification and salary schedules for fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 21, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the October 21, 2026 Saratoga City Council meeting listed routine approvals, such as past meeting minutes and vendor payment records, along with final sign-off on two property splits. It also listed an annual update to the City Code and a proposal to begin forming a Climate Resilience District.
keyTopics: Council to consider approving the minutes of the September 30 special meeting and the October 7 regular meeting.
Council to review and accept the vendor payment check registers dated October 1 and October 8, 2026.
Final map approval for splitting the property at 14860 Farwell Ave into two lots.
Final map approval for splitting the property at 18510 Sobey Rd into two lots.

Public hearing on the 2026 annual City Code update, covering changes to scheduling appeals and qualifications for City Commissioners, among other topics; the agenda also listed resolutions to create a Climate Resilience District Task Force and start the process of establishing a Climate Resilience District.

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026 Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business such as purchasing city vehicles and awarding contracts for a park expansion and a Police Department backup generator. It also listed a proposed salary amendment for the City Manager, an extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention and custodial facilities, and a presentation from Cal Water on water conservation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco for the Building B Park Expansion Project, not to exceed $166,225, with up to 10% in additional construction contingency.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator, with a construction contingency of up to 15%.

The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting an annual base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, plus an annual CPI/general salary adjustment provision starting July 2027.
The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance extending Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium related to detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures, a resolution on a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of VTA, and a resolution to buy three replacement maintenance vehicles and one piece of equipment.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 20, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine business such as approving minutes from the October 6 meetings, reviewing August financial reports, and ratifying bills and payroll. It also listed several items authorizing the Town Manager to sign or negotiate contracts and a lease amendment.
keyTopics: Approval of the minutes from the October 6, 2026 Town Council regular meeting and special meeting
Receipt of the August 2026 expenditure and revenue reports and the monthly financial and investment report
Approval and ratification of accounts payable check registers and the payroll report
Authorization for the Town Manager to execute a first amendment with Foster and Foster
Authorization for the Town Manager to enter into a three-year agreement and to negotiate and execute a lease amendment

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 28, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda listed a Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole meeting in San José to review the final agenda for the November 3, 2026 City Council meeting and the draft agenda for November 10, 2026. It also listed several items for consideration, including a study session on affordability, a council referral status report, and a topic on automated license plate readers.
keyTopics: The agenda listed review of the November 3, 2026 final agenda and the November 10, 2026 draft agenda, including adding new items and assigning 'time certain' slots if needed.
A study session on 'Improving Affordability for San José Residents' was listed, presented by the City Manager.

The agenda listed retroactive approval of various special events sponsored by Council District 8 as City Council Sponsored Special Events, allowing the use of City funds and acceptance of donations of materials and services (Candelas).
The Annual City Council Referral Status Report for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 was listed from the City Manager.
An item on Automated License Plate Readers and a Deferred Compensation Advisory Committee appointment (Human Resources) were also listed.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 27, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026 Mountain View City Council meeting listed a closed-door session on City Attorney employment matters, followed by a regular session with student recognitions, a proclamation, and several city project and housing items. Items before the Council included a LinkedIn development agreement amendment, tax-exempt bond financing for a housing project on San Antonio Road, and plans for a highway interchange and the new Public Safety Building.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a 5:15 p.m. closed session on labor negotiations and the public employee appointment for the City Attorney position.
Mayor for a Day certificates of recognition were listed for Simon Kensky (elementary school) and Yichen Yang (middle school), along with a Breast Cancer Awareness Month proclamation.
A second reading of an amendment to the LinkedIn development agreement covering 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue was on the agenda.
Tax-exempt bond financing for a multi-family housing project at 334 San Antonio Road was listed for consideration.

The agenda included the design concept for State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange improvements (Project 19-65), pre-qualification of bidders and subcontractors for the Public Safety Building (Project 20-49), and adoption of a Public Art Strategy.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 27, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda listed a 6 p.m. closed-session special meeting followed by the regular 7 p.m. Council meeting for Oct. 27, 2026. Items on the agenda included a homelessness services contract extension, a purchase of three new fire trucks, new school speed zones, a ban on using drinking water to irrigate decorative grass, and a proposed rewrite of local rules for backyard housing and lot splits.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract amendment with WeHOPE for street outreach, a temporary hotel program, mobile hygiene services and an inclement weather hotel program, with a total not-to-exceed amount of $3,255,267.36 and an extension through Sept. 10, 2027.
The agenda listed a $7,372,642.10 purchase order to Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. for three Pierce 100-foot tower fire apparatuses.
The agenda listed a proposed ordinance to repeal and replace Sunnyvale's Dual Urban Opportunity (DUO) housing and Urban Lot Split rules and conform other zoning and fee provisions to new state laws.
The agenda listed a resolution to establish 15 mph school zones and extend the school zone near Laurelwood Elementary School.
The agenda listed an ordinance implementing AB 1572 to prohibit using potable water to irrigate nonfunctional turf.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 20, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the Cupertino City Council's October 20, 2026 meeting listed a regular session at 6:45 PM, along with a separately noticed special meeting at 5:45 PM that included a study session. Items before the Council included a bridge design contract, a plan for leasing a city-owned commercial property, a General Plan update on health and safety, and an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement.
keyTopics: McClellan Road Bridge Project: a proposal to accept $850,000 in federal grant funds and award a design services agreement to Biggs Cardoza Associates, Inc. for up to $1,278,700
A proposed approach for leasing the city-owned commercial property at 22100 Stevens Creek Boulevard
A public hearing on amendments to the Health and Safety chapter of the General Plan, including noise, geologic and seismic hazard appendices and a new Health and Safety Background Report
A public hearing on conduit financing for The RISE Block 5 Apartments Project, postponed from the October 6 meeting

Consent calendar items including a gymnastics classes and camps contract with Bay Aerials Gymnastics (up to $480,000, extendable to $800,000 over five years) and a first amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement with Tina Kapoor

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — October 20, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda for this October 20, 2026 special meeting of the Santa Clara City Council listed an update on an investigation into FIFA risk analysis disclosures, along with requests from two councilmembers to schedule future discussions. Those requests cover data centers and electricity demand, and apartment parking rules. The meeting was set for 5:30 pm in City Hall Council Chambers and by Zoom, with options for residents to submit written comments.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an update on the FIFA Risk Analysis Disclosures Investigation.

Councilmember Hardy's request to put a future item on the agenda asking staff for an update within 30 days on how the city approves and allocates power to new large electricity users, including data centers, with a possible pause (moratorium) on new stand-alone data centers. This item was deferred from October 6, 2026.

Councilmember Hardy's request to schedule a discussion of a policy that would bar the city from signing non-disclosure agreements with stand-alone data centers. This item was also deferred from October 6, 2026.

Councilmember Park's request to schedule a future discussion on how apartment residents could park in or near their complexes without fear of being ticketed or towed. This item was deferred from September 22 and October 6, 2026.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026 Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business such as meeting calendars and minutes, along with a proposed contract change for a new park design, a presentation on mosquito control, and a proposal to rename two city sites and name a new community garden. It also listed the annual review of the city's advisory commissions and their plans for the coming year.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an amendment to the design contract with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park, for an amount not to exceed $130,000.

A resolution on the agenda would rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden to "Milpitas Community Garden," rename Cesar Chavez Plaza to "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and name the garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District was listed to give a presentation to the Council.

The Council was scheduled to consider accepting the FY2025-26 annual report from city commissions and approving FY2026-27 work plans for eight commissions, including the Arts Commission, Economic Development and Trade Commission, and Library and Education Advisory Commission.
Routine items listed included the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, the October 6, 2026 meeting minutes, and lists of upcoming and Councilmember-requested agenda items.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — October 26, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for the October 26, 2026 Palo Alto City Council meeting listed a mix of routine appointments and consent items alongside several policy items, including winter storm preparedness, stream corridor protections, a pause on new detention facilities, and a proposed expansion of human services funding. The agenda also listed a closed-session discussion about the price and payment terms for a property at 1900 Embarcadero Road.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a review of the city's 2026-2027 winter storm preparedness activities, with a staff presentation and public comment.
The agenda listed a proposed expansion of the Human Services Resource Allocation Process (HSRAP) for FY 2028-2029, with $428,000 in additional annual funding.
The agenda listed a temporary ordinance to impose a moratorium on new or expanded detention and custodial facilities within Palo Alto city limits, with public comment.
The agenda listed an ordinance amending the Stream Corridor Protection section of the municipal code (18.40.140), with a supplemental report added, a staff presentation, and public comment.

The agenda listed a closed-session conference with real property negotiators about the price and payment terms for 1900 Embarcadero Road, with BioScience Property Investments named as the negotiating party.
